glossary.definition: An LLM key can use one external inspector in AI Guard; the lab models Model Armor first, with Azure AI Content Safety and Bedrock Guardrails as stub alternatives. A key has one: selecting another replaces the first. The lab's inspectors are stubs with fixed rules and say nothing about any vendor's detection.

The authority setting decides whether the inspector's findings enforce or only advise. Enforcing: a finding blocks the call. Advisory: the same finding is logged and the call goes through. The cap existing is from the 2026-11-21 release notes; what a blocked or logged call looks like is the lab's own model.

What the key does when its inspector is unreachable or too slow: closed blocks the call, open lets it through and the gateway log says so. Whether the product offers either is UNVERIFIED; the lab shows both as two configurations.

A refusal or error that carries its own code and says it came from the gateway (blocked_by_inspector, inspector_unavailable, inspector_timeout, inspector_malformed_findings, two_inspectors). Unreadable findings are always a named error, never a pass. The codes and statuses are the lab's own and UNVERIFIED.

Anything the release notes do not say is the lab's own model and is labelled UNVERIFIED: the category names (Model Armor's follow Google's public overview and need re-checking), fail-open or fail-closed, the timeout, what a client receives, whether the response is inspected, and the finding shape.

cards.label: S01: A harmless prompt passes the inspector
cards.description: The gateway inspects the prompt on the way in and the answer on the way out. Neither has a finding, the client gets the answer, and the trace shows the three steps with their lab time.

cards.label: S02: A prompt injection is stopped by the gateway
cards.description: The inspector reports a prompt injection finding and the key is enforcing, so the gateway answers with its own named refusal. The model is never called and no tokens are spent.

cards.label: S03: A card number in the prompt never reaches the model
cards.description: The inspector reports sensitive data and the enforcing key blocks the call. The number is masked everywhere the lab shows the prompt, and the model is not called.

cards.label: S04: A card number in the model's answer is caught on the way out
cards.description: The response inspection finds the sensitive data and the gateway withholds the answer. The model had already answered, so the tokens are spent: a response block costs what the call cost.

cards.label: S05: A link on the stub's list is blocked
cards.description: The inspector reports a malicious URL finding and the enforcing key blocks the call. The list is the lab's own, made of reserved .invalid names, and says nothing about real threat intelligence.

cards.label: S06: Advisory authority logs the finding; enforcing blocks it again
cards.description: The authority cap holds the inspector advisory: the same finding is written to the gateway log and the call goes through. Switching the key back to enforcing blocks the very same prompt.

cards.label: S07: The inspector is down: fail closed blocks, fail open lets it through
cards.description: With fail closed even a harmless prompt is blocked with a named error. With fail open the call goes through and the gateway log says it failed open. Whether the product offers both is not known.

cards.label: S08: A slow inspector hits its timeout
cards.description: The gateway gives up at the key's timeout on the lab clock. It is a timeout, not a finding: closed blocks the call, open lets it through, whatever the prompt holds.

cards.label: S09: Unreadable findings are a named error, never a pass
cards.description: The gateway returns the named error inspector_malformed_findings and does not call the model. Neither fail open nor advisory authority turns it into a pass.

cards.label: S10: A second inspector replaces the first
cards.description: Selecting the second inspector replaces the first and says which one went. The same prompt now comes back with the second inspector's own category names.

cards.label: S11: Two inspectors at once are refused
cards.description: The request is refused with the named error two_inspectors and the key keeps what it had: the next prompt is still inspected by the first inspector.

cards.label: What is sourced and what is the lab's model
cards.description: The release-notes claims, the lab's own model and the list of what is UNVERIFIED.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
